verdicts.summary: The note's only real hazard is that the work before closeRun is unbounded: the mutex, onShutdown, and the restartFiber interrupt. Finding 0 already states this. The timeout path itself (forkIn parentScope, then timeoutOption) behaves as the note describes.

The 5s value is passed correctly and the timeout path is handled. On timeout, stop() returns early and skips cleanup. The only things skipped are removeControlSource and discardSession, which just clears an in-memory session Ref, so nothing is lost when the process is quitting. The layer finalizer at line 1157 re-closes the run. A drain longer than 5s can trip the timeout, but at quit the only cost is a cut-off log tail. The lack of a log on timeout is a small diagnostics gap, not a correctness bug.

The open question is now answered: prepareRuntime at DesktopBackendConfiguration.ts:363 runs inside resolveWslStartConfig. That function is called from resolvePrimary when WSL-only is on (line 795) and from resolveWsl (line 862). start() holds the mutex across configResolve, so stop({timeout}) can block unbounded on the mutex. This is exactly finding 0.
